'''Tournament Guidelines''' is the procedure document for running a Star Wars CCG event.

* Decipher issued a tournament guide (PDF / HTML / text). The 15 April 1997 printing is linked from the 1998 [https://web.archive.org/web/19981205173603/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/overview/index.html overview] page. A later shared CCG guide sat on tournaments.decipher.com as tournamentguide-stswyj.
* The Players Committee document in force is [https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Star-Wars-CCG-Tournament-Guide-2.2.pdf Official Tournament Guide 2.2] (revised July 2018).


== Players Committee changes ==

* '''2003.''' The Players Committee's four-level Championship Circuit: Level 1 State, National and Provincial Championships (six to eight games of Swiss and a top-2 final; the winner qualified for Day 2 of Worlds), Level 2 Open Qualifiers (eight games and a top-4 playoff; top 2 to Day 2), Level 3 DPC Championship Series events with DeckTech (top 2 to Day 2), and Level 4 the World Championship.<ref name="pc-road03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030424052746/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/roadtoworlds03.htm Road to Worlds Begins in 2003], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 24 April 2003.</ref> Team tournaments at Origins, Gen Con and Dragon*Con in 2003 were to qualify players for a planned 2004 Regional Team Championship at Gen Con (teams of three from the same region).<ref name="pc-team03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030809101318/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/teamchampionship06122003.htm Team Championship Qualifiers Planned for 2003], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 9 August 2003.</ref> From 1 January 2003 Decipher ratings used a "K" value of 16 for local events, 32 for Level 1, 48 for Level 2 and 64 for Levels 3–4.<ref name="pc-champ0206">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030424053234/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/championshipnews02062003.htm 2003 Championship Circuit Opens in One Month], Andrew Howard, swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 24 April 2003.</ref>
* '''2004.''' The 2004 Championship Series (announced 18 February 2004) had Level 1 States, Provincials and Mini-Opens (winner's bye), Level 2 DPCs, Level 3 Nationals, Continentals, Invitationals and Majors (winner and runner-up byes), and Level 4 Worlds.<ref name="pc-int0404">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040415220046/http://swccgpc.com:80/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com news (December 2003 – April 2004)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 15 April 2004.</ref>
* '''2005.''' For Worlds 2005 qualifiers, "Tournament directors CANNOT play in their own qualifier, no matter the number of players or if it will avert a bye."<ref name="pc-worlds05">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041216041033/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/2005worlds.htm The Road to Worlds 2005], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 16 December 2004.</ref>
* '''1 April 2008.''' Changes announced by [[Michael Erisman]] for the Tournament Committee: a tournament director may play in his own event if he names an assistant judge and a back-up judge (a three-judge system), the event is not a constructed Championship-level event with a cash prize or several Day 2 byes, and he wins no prize other than tournament glass and Day 2 byes; and every Championship-level event must have at least six games.<ref name="pc-sid80">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080712072001/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=80 Changes to the Tournament Guide - Effect 4/1/08] (28 March 2008), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 12 July 2008.</ref>
